outcome: Incidence of refractory headache 72 hours after first dose
Incidences of side effects (nausea, vomiting, need for antiemetics, photophobia, neck stiffness)
cohort: Two hundred and ten American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status II women who complained of postdural puncture headache (PDPH) after obstetric spinal anesthesia.
finding: Adding either mirtazapine or sumatriptan to conventional management significantly reduced headache intensity, increased complete response rates, and decreased the incidence of refractory headaches 72 hours post-intervention compared to conventional management alone, with comparable efficacy between mirtazapine and sumatriptan.
